biography: Gerd Ruch's path to the DTM was paved with a restless energy that often landed him in trouble. Born in Ingolstadt, a stone's throw from Audi HQ, he spent his youth tearing around backroads in souped-up scooters, much to the dismay of the local constabulary. His father, a mechanic at Audi, recognized Gerd's raw talent, albeit channeled poorly. Seeing an opportunity to redirect this energy, he enrolled Gerd in a local karting academy at age 14. The transition wasn't seamless; Gerd's aggressive, almost reckless style resulted in numerous crashes and penalties. However, his sheer determination and undeniable speed caught the eye of an Audi junior team scout during a regional karting championship. After a meteoric rise through the Formula series, marked by both spectacular wins and equally spectacular DNFs, Ruch landed a seat in the Audi V8 quattro DTM squad. He's now a rising star, known for his audacious overtakes and willingness to push the limits, even if it means flirting with disaster. His current DTM season is a proving ground, with the pressure to convert raw potential into consistent results mounting each race weekend.
drivingStyle: Ruch's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He's known for late braking and aggressive corner entry speeds, often carrying more momentum than his tires can handle. This results in dramatic slides and near misses, but also allows him to pull off stunning overtakes. He struggles with tire management, often burning through his rubber early in a race, leaving him vulnerable in the later stages. Under pressure, Ruch tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes to his detriment, forcing errors that cost him positions. However, when he's on his game, he's a formidable competitor, capable of extracting every last ounce of performance from his machine.

rivalries.reason: Richter, a veteran DTM driver, publicly criticized Ruch's aggressive driving after a controversial incident at the Norisring where Ruch punted Richter off the track while attempting an overtake.
Moreau, a rising female star in the DTM, has consistently outperformed Ruch, fueling a competitive tension and a desire from Ruch to prove his superiority.
Enzo's calculated, methodical approach to racing directly contrasts Ruch's impulsive style, leading to frequent clashes on and off the track.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, inside out, for every race.
Listens to a specific German techno song on repeat for at least an hour before each race to get pumped up.
Refuses to eat anything green on race days, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. If you're not willing to risk it all, you don't deserve to win."
careerHighlight: Winning the ADAC Formula Masters championship in 2021, dominating the season with a string of pole positions and victories, solidifying his reputation as a future star.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Hockenheimring DTM race in 2023, costing him his first potential DTM victory and handing the win to his rival, Klaus Richter.
